transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come in?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I just keep forgetting things. Things I really shouldn't be forgetting. 

Like... missing my heart follow-up appointments, or forgetting to call the clinic back. Even just going to do a simple repair job and realizing I didn't bring the right tools with me. So... yeah, that's why I came in.
When did you first start noticing these memory problems? Did they come on suddenly over days or weeks, or have they been gradually getting worse over months or longer?

Well... I suppose it's been causing real trouble for about a year and two months. It wasn't overnight, just... got worse after I had a bit of a cardiac scare. 

They made me cut back on my walking, and the projects I used to do. Those things sort of... kept me settled, I guess. So, yeah. About fourteen months.

Around the time these memory problems started about 14 months ago, did you have any sudden illness, fever, head injury, or did your medications change? Or did anything else happen suddenly that you think might have triggered this?
No... no, nothing like that. Just the heart thing I mentioned. No head injury or fever or anything. And I think the pills are mostly the same. Just... just the memory stuff.
Have other people in your life—family, friends, coworkers—noticed these memory problems, or is it mainly something you've noticed about yourself?

Well... I suppose others have noticed. 

The guys at the senior center... we do repair projects together. They can't really count on me like they used to. And, like I said, the doctor's office... they've had to call and chase me down about those missed heart appointments. So... yeah. They've noticed.
On any given day, does your memory seem to fluctuate—like some days are better and some days are worse—or is it pretty consistently the same level of difficulty every day?
I don't really know... I haven't kept track of it like that. I guess it just seems about the same. I don't really notice if one day is better than another. It's just... always kind of a problem now.

Beyond forgetting things, have you noticed any changes in your ability to do everyday tasks—like managing your medications, handling your finances, cooking, or taking care of yourself? Or is it really just the memory and forgetting part?
I don't... I mean, I can still do things. I just forget sometimes. I take care of myself fine. It's really just the memory part.

You mentioned the memory problems started about 14 months ago after your heart problem. In those early weeks or months, did things feel confusing or foggy in your thinking, or did you feel disoriented or mixed up at any point—or was it just the forgetting from the start?
I don't think so. I wasn't... confused or anything like that. Just the forgetting. That's all I noticed.

When you had that cardiac scare 14 months ago, do you remember if you had a high fever, were very short of breath, felt severely confused, or had any other serious physical symptoms around the time the memory problems started—or did the memory issues just gradually develop over weeks after the heart event?

I don't remember any fever. It was just... my heart, so I don't know. I wasn't confused. I guess the memory thing just... started happening later on. I didn't really pay attention to exactly when it started.

When you think back to right after that cardiac scare—in the first week or two—did you notice the memory problems starting right away, or did it take several weeks or even months before you really started having trouble remembering things?
I really couldn't tell you. I... I wasn't keeping track of the days back then. It just sort of became an issue at some point. I don't know exactly when.

Right around the time of your cardiac scare 14 months ago, did anyone tell you that you seemed confused, disoriented, or 'not yourself' for a period of days or weeks—even if you don't remember feeling that way yourself?
No, nobody said anything like that to me. I was just... recovering. It was just the memory stuff later on. I didn't have people telling me I was acting strange or anything.

In the week or two right after your heart scare, did anyone—a family member, nurse, or doctor—notice that you were having trouble paying attention, seemed confused about where you were or what day it was, or seemed to drift in and out of alertness? Even if you don't remember it yourself?
No... I mean, like I said, nobody told me I was acting strange. I knew where I was. They just... they were focused on my heart. Nobody said anything about me drifting off or forgetting the day.

In those first few days or weeks after your heart problem, did you spend time in the hospital? And if so, did the nurses or doctors mention anything about you being confused, having trouble staying alert, or having a hard time paying attention during your recovery?
Yeah, I was in the hospital. But... no. Like I just said, they didn't mention anything about me being confused or... not paying attention. They were just treating my heart. That's it.

During your hospital stay for the heart problem, do you remember the doctors or nurses ever waking you up to check on you, or do you remember being alert and able to talk with them? Or is that time kind of fuzzy in your memory?
No, it wasn't fuzzy. I remember it fine. They woke me up to check my blood pressure and things, sure, but... I was awake. I talked to them just fine. It was just normal hospital stuff.

When you were in the hospital for your heart, do you remember if your thinking felt clear the whole time, or were there any moments where things felt a bit hazy, confused, or like you weren't quite yourself—even if it only lasted a few hours?

I... look, I don't really know how else to say it. My thinking was clear. I wasn't hazy at all. I just... I felt normal. Honestly, I just wanted to get out of that bed and go home. But my head was fine.
